quite interested in how the troops reacted. I didn't find any soldier there who was afraid.
They were all the ones who hadn't seen a bomb before. They were a little apprehensive,
but there was no fire relief when the thing went off. And no great exuberance which comes
from falling being scared. In other words, as far as they sold your actions, the thing
I would say it, they took it and they strayed as American soldiers take all things of danger
or things that they have been told about and oriented on. The troops moved out just as soon
as the safety officers pronounced it safe and went out and get formation. Last I saw
them, they were pretty well up towards ground zero.
Alright, thank you very much. Bill Hodge, what would you say was the main reaction of the
troops there in the trenches as they were waiting for the bomb to go off? Well, they reaction
the troops and the trenches. They did exactly what they were told to do. They showed good discipline,
which was good sense in this case. Any man stuck his head up, there was trouble in store
for him. And they seemed to take all of this, very well. They did indeed. And how did they
move out when the order was to give and move out until we got very proper and good formation?
And they maintained tight formation. And you think that this training that they have received,
that you have received the training that these men got there, will have to be beneficial
in any other time that they may come across atomic attacks? Yes, it will be beneficial
to them and all sort of their buddies when they go back to units so they can tell them
about this thing. We would need trained soldiers now that atomic weapons are definitely here.
We certainly need to train soldiers to know what to do and to pass the word on not only
to the people in the armed forces but the civilians as well. That is correct. And we need
the soldier to understand this weapon so we can use it and tell you. Any other thing that
you would like to bring out about?
